claims.statement: Taiwan's geopolitical risk index reached a historic peak in March 2026, with 0.3339% of newspaper articles covering Taiwan-related geopolitical tensions, the highest level in the entire 10-year data series.

Taiwan experienced an extreme geopolitical risk spike in May 2026, with 0.5347% of articles focused on Taiwan, representing the single highest monthly reading in the dataset and more than double the typical 2024-2025 baseline.
The global geopolitical risk index surged to 330.1768 in March 2026, exceeding the previous peak of 318.9549 in March 2022 during the Ukraine invasion, with Taiwan featuring prominently in coverage.

Taiwan's geopolitical risk remained elevated in October 2026 at 0.0821% of articles, though substantially lower than the March-May 2026 crisis period, indicating a partial de-escalation but continued elevated baseline.

Taiwan's geopolitical risk index showed a sustained elevation throughout 2022-2026, averaging approximately 0.25% of articles compared to 0.08% in 2017-2020, representing a structural tripling of baseline risk.
The August 2022 spike to 0.7402% of articles represented the previous all-time high for Taiwan geopolitical risk before being exceeded in May 2026, marking two distinct crisis episodes.
Taiwan's historical geopolitical risk index (3-newspaper series) reached 0.5016% in May 2026, confirming the severity of the crisis across both contemporary and historical newspaper sources.

Following the May 2026 peak, Taiwan's geopolitical risk declined sharply to 0.1807% in June and 0.0821% by October, suggesting a rapid de-escalation of the immediate crisis but persistence above pre-2021 levels.

summary: Taiwan experienced an unprecedented geopolitical crisis in early 2026, with risk indicators reaching historic peaks [geopolitical:TWN:001][geopolitical:TWN:002][geopolitical:TWN:007]. The country's GPR index surged to 0.5347% of newspaper articles in May 2026, the highest level ever recorded in the dataset and more than double typical 2024-2025 levels [geopolitical:TWN:002]. This followed an initial spike in March 2026 when both Taiwan's country-specific index (0.3339%) and the global GPR index (330.18) reached extreme levels, surpassing even the March 2022 Ukraine invasion peak [geopolitical:TWN:001][geopolitical:TWN:003]. The crisis appears to have partially de-escalated by October 2026, with Taiwan's index declining to 0.0821%, though this remains elevated compared to pre-2021 baseline levels [geopolitical:TWN:004][geopolitical:TWN:008]. Taiwan's geopolitical risk profile has undergone a structural shift since 2021, with the baseline tripling from approximately 0.08% in 2017-2020 to around 0.25% in 2022-2026 [geopolitical:TWN:005]. The May 2026 event represents the second major crisis episode, following the August 2022 spike to 0.7402% [geopolitical:TWN:006].
